subject: Life Skills
title: Deep Work vs. Shallow Work
description: A 60-second lesson on Deep Work vs. Shallow Work.

hook.text: Cal Newport noticed that professors who published the most spent fewer hours working — but more hours focused.

buildup.text: Deep work is cognitively demanding, distraction-free effort. Shallow work is email, scheduling, and busywork.

discovery.text: You can sustain about four hours of true deep work per day. Beyond that, quality drops sharply for most people.

twist.text: Most jobs reward shallow work with visible responsiveness. Deep work is invisible but produces all the real value.

climax.text: Block your best four hours for deep work. Guard them like a meeting with your career's most important person.

punchline.text: Four focused hours beat twelve scattered ones.

quiz.question: How many hours of deep work can most people sustain daily?
